title.full: Global energy and climate outlook 2024 – Updating NDCs and closing the ambition gap – Indicators for 1.5°C alignment

name.full: Nationally Determined Contributions and Long-Term Strategies

description: Exploratory global pathway. All countries achieve NDCs and long-term carbon neutrality pledges.
pathwayDescription: The European Commission’s Global Energy and Climate Outlook 2024 (GECO) provides an ensemble of energy transition scenarios, developed by the Joint Research Centre. Its Nationally Determined Contribution – Long Term Strategies (NDC-LTS) pathway provides a detailed exploratory scenario in which all countries fully implement their existing conditional and unconditional NDCs, as well as introducing additional policies necessary to achieve stated long-term carbon neutrality objectives. These policies reduce emissions significantly from GECO’s reference pathway, producing a projected temperature rise of 1.8°C by 2100.

coreDrivers.policies: The pathway is aligned with Nationally Determined Contributions and Long-Term Strategies (NDC-LTS). It also adds country-specific carbon prices and regulatory instruments to meet NDCs and LTS pledges until 2050.
coreDrivers.emissionsTargets: National NDC objectives and long-term net-zero/neutrality pledges constrain emissions, yielding about 1.8°C warming.
coreDrivers.technologyCosts: Technology learning rates are endogenously developed in the model, based on learning curve literature. The overall technology cost trend decreases based on the adoption of individual technologies and their unit costs.
coreDrivers.macroeconomicDrivers: Population and GDP assumptions are shared across the GECO scenarios and set the activity baseline. Inputs combine World Bank, IMF, OECD/SSP2, EU Ageing Report, and JRC-IIASA sources.

dependencies.dependency_description: NDC/LTS targets and country-specific carbon prices materially drive power outcomes with exogenous capacity additions and technology mix inputs.

Quantitative fuel prices and power-mix projections indicate that country-specific carbon prices and policy targets alter relative fossil and low-carbon economics. However costs plays a limited role in the scenario as most of the capacity additions are made per each countries' target.
Renewables technology mix targets imply additional grid flexibility and transmission infrastructure, but this is not quantified in the scenario.

byMetric.scopeLimitations: CO2 from fuel combustion in power generation and district heating are combined, the heat share is not separable. Non-CO2 gases are not included. There is no on-grid/captive/rooftop split stated.

geography: Rest of Commonwealth of Independent States
byMetric.scopeLimitations: Installed generation capacity (GW) by technology, fossil generation is split into unabated and with-CCUS. Storage is modelled but reported only as share of electricity delivered from storage. Dedicated renewables for hydrogen and DAC are reported separately and excluded from the total.
